Keeping this feature going seems like common sense to preserve the sites integrity and freedom from manipulation.

I wanted to upvote a comment, but when I clicked the upvote button, I was told I needed one comment contribution point to upvote. That seems reasonable, 1 point is easy to get.

But then, I tried downvoting the same comment to see if it was the same system for downvotes. But for downvotes, I need 100 contribution points. That takes a much longer time.

I was disappointed by this because this website's emphasis on free speech is what intrigued me. Votes are speech, both upvotes and downvotes. You're saying "This is good" or "this is not good".

I'm not bringing this up because I have an urge to downvote comments; I'm bringing it up because there should be no interference with free speech on this website. Even negatice votes. ALL users deserve a voice to vote on submissions. Not just users that have been around for a while, or just users that the community approves of and upvotes often.

Effectively, this system says that popular users have more important opinions. Free speech means free speech. I came here because reddit has been filled with censorship. I came here expecting free speech. Downvote restrictions like these will ruin this website.
Allow downvoting for all users, or at least lower the required contribution points needed

While I understand your concern and fully support the idea that all users should be equal, I would like to explain that this restriction was put into place because downvoting was heavily abused by newcommers: ranging from 4chan users to bots, everyone was downvoting everything, regardless of content or contribution value.

At first, downvotes were being given through user profile pages where newcommers downvoted everything, entire comment/submission histories in matter of minutes. This made us disable voting on user profiles.

If we take a look at a real world example, you will find that people do not have the right to vote until they reach a certain age. In most countries this age is 18 or so. Why should we not apply the same principle here and convert age to comment contribution points?

The amount of comment contribution points required is certainly open for debate, but removal of this restriction would pretty much open up whoaverse to downvoting brigades and all sorts of childish behavior that would degrade the quality of whoaverse overall.
Keeping this feature going seems like common sense to preserve the sites integrity and freedom from manipulation.

After spending an entire day working on this feature, it is finally live and available to everyone. You should now be able to send a private message to anyone, receive, and have a view for inbox and sent messages.

The mail icon should light up (red) when you have a new unread message.

For now, you will not be able to delete or reply using action buttons under each message, but you can compose new messages.

This is the first step towards a full-fledged private messaging system which will, when fully implemented, offer comment replies, user mentions, submission replies and some other perks.

Please test it out and report back in case you discover anything weird :)

Please remember that private messages are not encrypted in whoaverse database, so even though they are called "private", you should be aware that they are stored in plain text.
